content="Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only known world to support life. It is about 4.5 billion years old, and its age is estimatedfrom radiometric dating of ancient rocks and meteorites. Roughly 71 percent of its surface is covered by water, mostly in oceans. The planet has a solid iron-rich core, a liquid outer core that generates its magnetic field, a thick mantle, and a thin crust. Earth's atmosphere is about 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen, with trace gases like argon and carbon dioxide. The planet takes about 365.25 days to orbit the Sun, which is why we have leap years every four years. Earth rotates once roughly every 24 hours, and this rotation causes the cycle of day and night. Its magnetic field shields the surface from much of the solar wind and harmful charged particles. The surface is divided into several large tectonic plates that slowly move,shaping mountains, volcanoes, and earthquakes over millions of years. Earth is the densest planet in the Solar System, and it is the largest of the four rocky inner planets."
